OCD Live

The booking site Bovann asked for: book a 1h30 live at the OCD Live studio in Lomé, or remotely from 17 countries, on the House of Challenge TikTok account, with the seller's number and address on screen, a notification to Bovann Group and a control room. Then a business page, invoices, expenses, an AI agent, an academy and a 304-page book read in the app.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem

Bovann leads the OCD movement on TikTok and opened the House of Challenge account to every OCD who wants to sell. He asked for a booking site from end to end: choose the studio or a remote live, pick a day and a time, pay, and let Bovann Group know who is coming, what they sell and when. A seller alone outside needs to be seen first: the product, the phone number and the address in front of a large audience, the marketing before the sale.

02

What it does

Six steps to book: studio or remote, day, time, package, business details with consent to show the number and address, then mobile money. The seller gets a ticket with a QR code and Bovann Group gets the notification Bovann described. The team space has a dashboard, the studio schedule and the on-screen banner, a screen for the host who brings remote sellers on air at their local time, the sellers, the payments and editable prices. After the live, each seller has a public page with a QR code, payment links, invoices and quotes in FCFA, expenses from receipt photos, an agent with 12 skills that prepares and never sends anything without approval, a 60-lesson academy and the OCD room.

03

How it is built

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no framework, so it opens fast on a phone with a slow connection. In the demo each account's data stays in the browser. The agent uses Claude when it is available and prepared answers otherwise. Payments are mapped by country: KPay for Cameroon (MTN MoMo, Orange Money and cards); elsewhere the country's operators, such as Flooz, T-Money, Wave, Airtel Money or MonCash, through a local provider still to choose. The map of Africa and the patterns, kente, bogolan, ndop and sixteen more, are drawn in code. The two request videos were transcribed on the machine, and the book was written from them and set from Markdown into an A5 PDF with Chrome; the book's text loads only when someone opens it.
